key_insight: FAMOS can infer an object’s movable parts and joint parameters from a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds, instead of depending on a single view and heavy shape priors. By reasoning across multiple observations, it improves articulation modeling from limited evidence.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of recovering 3D articulation for objects when only sparse monocular observations are available, where each view shows incomplete geometry and motion cues.
method: Takes a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds as input rather than a single observation.
Jointly predicts movable-part segmentation and joint parameters in a feed-forward manner.
Aggregates evidence across multiple observations to reason about object articulation with less reliance on category-level priors.
impact: This is useful for AI/ML practitioners working in 3D perception, robotics, and scene understanding because it enables more reliable articulation estimation from limited data. It could improve downstream tasks like object manipulation, reconstruction, and motion-aware perception.
visual_elements: Input-to-output pipeline showing sparse point clouds leading to part segmentation and joint prediction

paper_title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
paper_authors: Kevin Qu, Tao Sun, Massimiliano Viola, Liyuan Zhu, Zhizhuo Zhou
